newsitem.title: CHINA: China says foreign firms seek LNG development role.
newsitem.headline: China says foreign firms seek LNG development role.

text.p: At least 10 foreign companies have expressed interest in taking a role in possible large-scale development of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in southern China, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The newspaper did not name any of the companies or give details of the expressions of interest.

But it quoted Chen Bingqian, vice president of China National Offshore Oil Corp, as saying the company was conducting feasibility studies on LNG development on behalf of the State Planning Commission.
The newspaper, published by the official China Daily, did not give a timetable for any decisions.
It said, however, that once a decision was made, the government would order build a port terminal to receive and treat LNG. It would also order transport vehicles.
China produced 8.225 billion cubic metres of natural gas from January through April 1997, up 10.7 percent compared with the same period in 1996, according to the State Statistical Bureau.
